full_judgment: 5. The Additional Sessions Judge has next observed that only six witnesses out of all mentioned in the petition of complaint were examined in support of the complaint's case and the rest were withheld without any satisfactory explanation and that this would lead to an adverse presumption against the complainant's case. The learned Judge is obviously wrong in taking the aforesaid view. It is not necessary that all the witnesses cited in the petition of complaint should be examined. The important point for consideration is whether upon the basis of the evidence on record the order of conviction can be supported or not. It is not always the member of the witnesses but the quality tab courts in determining whether the prosecution case is acceptable or not. The learned judge has taken exception again for not examining P.W. 1 Hurmat (it should be Md. Hekmatulla Mondal as cited in the petition of complaint and not P.W. 1.) The non-examination of Hekmat Ullah Mondal who is the paternal uncle of the complainant, in my opinion, has not affected the complainant's case in the least, for there is sufficient evidence or record to prove that the complainant's father and uncle took settlement of some lands including the case land from the Government and the complaint was in possession thereof in pursuance of an amicable partition between his father and uncles. The learned Judge wrongly found that P.W. 3 did not support the fact of Salish. I find from his cross examination that he clearly stated that he was present in the Sandi. P.W. 6, of course, started that there was no Salish over the occurrence but in another part of his cross examination he stated that he did not go to the Madrasa on the date of occurrence. The Salish, according to the other witnesses, took place at the Madrasa on the date of occurrence. It was not, therefore, unlikely for P.W. 6 not to know about the Salish since he admittedly did not go to the Madrasa on that day. The other omissions as referred to with regard to the evidence of PWs. 2 and 3 and the admission by P.W. 4 are not at all material for deciding the points at issue. The admission of P.W. 4 is not inconsistent with the complainant's case in that the original plot was a big one and that settlements were taken by the complainant's father and his uncles and the accused persons of the different parts thereof.
